title: AI-based prognosis and chemotherapy benefit in node-positive, HR+ breast cancer: a blinded external validation on SWOG-8814 trial
summary: Results/Abstract: in the multi-modal score, DFS association HR 1.60 (95% CI 1.44–1.78) and C-index 0.66 versus 0.59 for histology-only. Chemotherapy-benefit interaction was exploratory and did not meet conventional significance (p=0.053); only the prognostic result supports approval. This is the result-bearing preprint version dated 2026-10-23; peer-review status is not established by the reviewed source.
ai_technology: Methods/Abstract: locked Ataraxis Breast CTX scores use H&E whole-slide pathology alone or combined with clinical variables; trial data were not used for retraining and predictions were blinded to outcome.
organization: Indiana University; Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center; Loyola University Chicago Stritch School of Medicine; Ataraxis AI; University of Alabama at Birmingham; University of Michigan Medical School; Emory University; University of Kansas Medical Center

evidence.tested: Results/Abstract: in the multi-modal score, DFS association HR 1.60 (95% CI 1.44–1.78) and C-index 0.66 versus 0.59 for histology-only. Chemotherapy-benefit interaction was exploratory and did not meet conventional significance (p=0.053); only the prognostic result supports approval. Methods, “Study design and population”: blinded external evaluation in 677 of 1,477 participants from phase III randomized SWOG-8814, with outcome analysis by SWOG; DFS primary endpoint. The 677-sample digitized-slide subset is 46% of trial cohort; not prospective contemporary clinical utility.
